original.target_description: Study 1, whole-sample agreement in intentionality ratings across 20 behaviors: average correlation of each participant with the remaining group.

n.sample_role: Participants pooled across San Jose State and Stanford undergraduate samples, rating 20 behaviors
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this test in original methods. Original methods give component samples of 56 and 48; total 104 is explicitly printed by replication authors in Table 2.
n.location: Chandrashekar et al. (2022), p. 4, Table 2, Sample size row, Original study column; original methods p. 103

es.location: p. 104 (PDF p. 4), Results, continuation from p. 103
es.quote: average correlation of r (20) 5 .80 with the remaining group

p.location: pp. 103–104, Study 1 Results; no p value printed for the average rater–whole correlation

replication.target_description: Replication Study 2, whole-sample agreement in intentionality ratings across 20 behaviors: average correlation of each participant with the remaining group.

n.sample_role: Participants: US American MTurk participants retained for analysis, rating 20 behaviors
n.exclusions: 835 recruited; 18 excluded: eight incomplete and ten reporting English understanding lower than 5 on a 7-point scale.
n.location: p. 2, section 3.2.2; p. 4, Table 2, Sample size row

es.location: p. 3, section 4.1; p. 4, Table 2, Study 2 column, Average rater–whole correlation

p.location: p. 3, section 4.1 and p. 4, Table 2; no p value printed for the average rater–whole correlation

reported_success.location: p. 4, section 5 Discussion (joint verdict for both replications; footnote 6 prioritizes Study 2)
reported_success.quote: Our replication results support the original study's central argument.

notes: Selected average rater–whole correlation because original locator PDF p. 4 directly reports .80; the neutral agreement description also encompasses average pairwise inter-rater correlation, which is a different summary (.64 original; .40 Study 1; .59 Study 2). No p values were printed for these descriptive agreement measures, and none was inferred. Original total n is an explicitly author-supplied value in the replication paper, checked against the two original participant samples; no conversion was performed. Authors qualify the joint replication verdict by basing main conclusions on Study 2 because Study 1 is small. PDF text parses original equals signs as 5; the quote preserves the frozen parse.
